title: Action log record
description: One completed step of one run, as written to actions.jsonl. This file is the contract between the writer and everything that reads a run afterwards -- the replayer, the benchmark, the span exporter -- so a field removed here is a field those readers lose for every run already on disk.

step_id.description: Stable id for this step, unique within the run and referenced by every call the step made.

number.description: Position in the run, counting from 1. Step 0's opening navigation is recorded on the run, not here.

started_at.description: When the step began: the moment the planner was first asked.

ended_at.description: When the step was recorded, after its action was executed.

observation.description: The page this step was decided against.

action.description: The action performed, or null for a step whose every planning attempt was refused.
Which of the seven actions this is.

result.description: What came of performing the action, or null for a step that performed none and for the final done.

status.description: How the execution ended, in the executor's own vocabulary.

attempts.description: Planning attempts this step took. More than one means the validator sent the planner back.

rejections.description: Why each refused attempt was refused, in order. Empty on a step approved first time.

forced.description: Why the controller replaced the planner's action, or empty when it did not.

screenshot_decision.description: Whether this step's observation carried an image, and the rule that decided it. Null when the run had no gate.

calls.description: Every model call this step made, refused attempts included.

identifier.description: A kind-prefixed random id. The prefix means a bare id in a log line says what it points at.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. Always a point in time and never a duration: a duration cannot be turned back into a position on the run's timeline.

url.description: The page's address at the moment it was read.

elements.description: The interactive elements found in the viewport, numbered as the planner saw them.

text.description: The distilled page text the planner was shown.

text_truncated.description: Whether that text hit its budget and was cut.

screenshot.description: Path to the annotated screenshot this step carried into the prompt, or null when the cost gate kept it out or the endpoint cannot see images. Null here is not a claim that no image was taken -- see screenshot_on_disk.

screenshot_on_disk.description: Path to this step's annotated screenshot, whether or not it went to the model. The one a person opens when reading the run afterwards, and written on every step of every run that had somewhere to put an image -- including runs against an endpoint that cannot see at all. Absent in traces written before the two were told apart.

call.description: One model call, as the cost log records it. The same records appear in calls.jsonl, flattened out of their steps.

call_id.description: Stable id for this call, unique within the run.

parent_step_id.description: The step this call was made during. What lets a flattened cost log be put back under its steps.

started_at.description: When the call was first attempted, waiting for a busy endpoint included.

profile.description: The endpoint profile that served the call.

model.description: The exact model the route resolved to, which on a vision step is not the profile's text model.

vision.description: Whether an image was part of the request.

prompt_tokens.description: Input tokens billed, or null if the endpoint reported none.

completion_tokens.description: Output tokens billed, or null if not reported.

latency_s.description: Seconds the attempt that worked took, with waiting kept out of it.

finish_reason.description: Why generation stopped. 'length' here explains a truncated action better than the parse failure it causes.

cost_usd.description: Dollars, or null where the route is free, self-hosted, or unpriced. Never 0.0 as a stand-in for unknown.

schema_enforced.description: Whether the endpoint was asked to constrain decoding to the schema, rather than merely shown one.

backoffs.description: Refusals this call survived before it went through, each with the pause it cost.
